references.title: Music organized by game usage
references.creator: Topfhelm
references.summary: A composer portfolio whose music is grouped by its role inside games instead of only by genre, release, or instrumentation.
references.takeaway: The listener immediately understands where each piece belongs: combat, exploration, character, atmosphere, interface, or narrative.
references.vois_application: Organize VOIS music by gameplay function, then show implementation context, adaptive behavior, and the scene or system each cue supports.

references.title: Clean level design portfolio with clear role separation
references.creator: Sean Gorman
references.summary: Level design portfolio organized by project, with explicit role, contributions, and process breakdown per piece.
references.takeaway: Separate projects cleanly, state your exact role, and let the viewer navigate by project rather than by skill.
references.vois_application: VOIS environment case studies (Nyelith Forest, dungeons) should each get a self-contained project card with role, constraints, and evidence.

references.title: Technical level design with responsibilities and tools
references.creator: Yoann Pierkot
references.summary: Portfolio emphasizing experience, responsibilities, and technical level design. Strong on process but light on systems/balance.
references.takeaway: Present responsibilities and technical decisions alongside the visual result — not just pretty maps.
references.vois_application: Room Gate authoring helper and foliage scatterer are natural VOIS technical-level-design evidence.

references.title: Gameplay, systems, and combat design in Unity and Unreal
references.creator: Germán López (Gerlogu)
references.summary: Among the closest references to VOIS direction: gameplay, systems, and combat design work across Unity and Unreal. Covers implementation and design reasoning.
references.takeaway: The sweet spot for VOIS: systems thinking paired with implementation evidence in real engines.
references.vois_application: Primary reference model for Timed Hit, Marks, and combat flow case studies. Study how he structures the designer-programmer hybrid narrative.

references.title: Professional breakdowns with design goals and ownership
references.creator: Oliver William Walker
references.summary: Strong professional breakdowns: design objectives, content, gameplay scripting, iteration process, and ownership within commercial projects.
references.takeaway: Always state the design goal before showing the solution. Ownership clarity builds credibility.
references.vois_application: Apply his goal → content → iteration → result structure to VOIS combat and systems features.

references.title: How to present prototypes, technical implementation, and system interaction
references.creator: VG Entertainment
references.summary: Guide for presenting mechanic prototypes, technical implementation details, and interaction with other systems in a technical design portfolio.
references.takeaway: Show the prototype, the technical decisions, and how the system talks to other systems — not just the polished result.
references.vois_application: Use as structural reference for VOIS technical design case studies (event routing, persistence, authoring tools).

references.title: Structure every piece: context, process, decisions, contribution, result
references.creator: Alexia Mandeville
references.summary: Guide for structuring each portfolio piece with visual context, process, design decisions, personal contribution, and final result.
references.takeaway: The five-part structure (context → process → decisions → contribution → result) works across every discipline.
references.vois_application: Adopt this as the default VOIS case study template. Every feature card should answer these five questions.

references.title: Define narrative, select pieces by opportunity, show skills and process
references.creator: Champlain College
references.summary: Guide for building a professional narrative, selecting portfolio pieces according to the role, and demonstrating skills through process documentation.
references.takeaway: Curate per audience. A combat designer portfolio and a tools portfolio should feel like different documents even if they share evidence.
references.vois_application: VOIS will eventually need discipline-specific views from the same evidence bank. This guide informs that filtering logic.

references.title: General portfolio guide with sections per design discipline
references.creator: Game Design Skills
references.summary: Comprehensive portfolio guide with dedicated sections for gameplay, systems, level, and narrative design portfolios.
references.takeaway: Different design disciplines need different evidence types. Don't use the same template for systems and level design.
references.vois_application: Use the discipline-specific sections to validate VOIS case study formats per angle (systems vs. combat vs. tools).

references.title: Present systems around desired experience, relationships, and analysis
references.creator: Game Design Skills
references.summary: Systems design portfolio guidance: organize around the desired player experience, show relationships between mechanics, and include systemic analysis.
references.takeaway: Systems portfolios fail when they list features. They succeed when they show how features produce player behavior.
references.vois_application: The Marks System and CP economy case studies should lead with the player decision, not the implementation.

references.title: Systems and game design portfolio (Game Design Skills)
references.creator: Dylan Del Sontro
references.summary: Systems and game design portfolio hosted on Game Design Skills. Additional example within the systems design reference.

references.title: Gameplay, systems, and UI portfolio (Game Design Skills)
references.creator: Chloe Ingram
references.summary: Portfolio spanning gameplay, systems, and UI design. Useful cross-discipline reference for VOIS features touching multiple domains.

references.title: Game design portfolio (Game Design Skills)
references.creator: André Salomão
references.summary: Game design portfolio on Game Design Skills platform. General reference for design presentation structure.

references.title: Detailed systems design deliverable with full documentation
references.creator: André Salomão / Project Ink
references.summary: Deep systems design deliverable showing full documentation of a game system. High-value reference for how to structure a VOIS systems case study.
references.vois_application: Potential template for VOIS Marks System or CP economy deep-dive case study.

references.title: Detailed case study breakdown (Game Design Skills)
references.creator: Carter Kappes
references.summary: Detailed case study for Tournamental on Game Design Skills. Reference for individual feature deep-dive structure.

principles.title: Organize by the viewer's decision
principles.description: A recruiter should not need to decode the project. Group work by the question they are trying to answer: Can this person design combat audio? Can they build a game system? Can they communicate visual intent?

principles.title: Show evidence, not only output
principles.description: Pair the polished result with constraints, iteration, implementation details, and a concise explanation of what changed because of your work.

principles.title: One VOIS feature can serve several portfolios
principles.description: A timed-hit feature can become a game-design case study, a programming breakdown, a UI interaction piece, and a sound-design implementation example. Reuse evidence, not identical framing.

principles.title: Capture while the work is alive
principles.description: Record before-and-after images, short clips, diagrams, commits, failed approaches, and final decisions during development. Reconstructing them months later is expensive.

principles.title: Separate reference from imitation
principles.description: Store the exact pattern you admired, the underlying principle, and a distinct VOIS application. This turns inspiration into reusable knowledge instead of a mood board.

principles.title: Every case study needs a proof package
principles.description: Minimum evidence: final media, problem statement, your role, constraints, process, technical or design decisions, result, and one concrete lesson.

principles.title: Structure every piece the same way
principles.description: Context → Process → Decisions → Contribution → Result. This five-part structure (from Alexia Mandeville) works across game design, programming, audio, and UI. Consistency helps evaluators compare pieces quickly.

principles.title: Curate per audience, not per project
principles.description: A combat designer portfolio and a tools portfolio should feel like different documents even when they share the same underlying evidence. Select and frame pieces according to the role you're targeting.

principles.title: State the design goal before the solution
principles.description: From Oliver William Walker: always anchor the work with what you were trying to achieve. The goal provides the lens through which every decision makes sense.

principles.title: Show how systems produce player behavior, not just features
principles.description: A systems portfolio fails when it lists mechanics. It succeeds when it demonstrates how features create specific player decisions, tensions, and experiences.

principles.title: Role clarity builds credibility
principles.description: From Sean Gorman: clean project separation with explicit role statements per piece. The viewer should never wonder what you actually did.

principles.title: Prioritize references that match your actual mix
principles.description: Gerlogu, Oliver William Walker, Sean Gorman, TopfHelm, Alexia Mandeville, and Project Ink cover systems design, implementation, process presentation, and contextual audio — the closest match to VOIS needs.
